newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HKMA says cautious on rapid HK May mortgage growth.
newsitem.headline: HKMA says cautious on rapid HK May mortgage growth.

text.p: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority expressed concerns on Thursday over the increase in residential mortgage lending in May.
"The rapid growth in residential mortgage lending in May gives some cause for concern," HKMA deputy chief executive David Carse said in a statement.
"However, the property market has recently been more subdued. The HKMA is therefore continuing to evaluate the situation," he said.

A latest survey by the HKMA said gross new loans increased during the month by 14.7 percent to HK$26 billion. The average size of new loans increased to HK$1.91 million compared with HK$1.77 million in April.
New loans approved during the month rose by 4.6 percent to HK$30.1 million.

Repayment of loans during May rose at a slower pace than new loans. The amount of outstanding loans thus increased by 2.7 percent to HK$371.8 billion in May, compared with a 2.4 percent increase in April, the statement said.
The annualised rate of growth of outstanding loans in the three months to May rose to 30 percent from 29.4 percent in the three months to April.
The average change over the last twelve months increased to 29.4 percent in May from 23.1 percent in April.
It said the trend of price cutting continued in May. Of new loans approved during May, 56.7 percent were priced at 0.25 percent above the best lending rate, compared with 55.4 percnt in April.
Gross loans for the purchase of properties in China decreased to HK$228 million in May from HK$238 million in April. The amount of outstanding loans increased by 1.08 percent to HK$6.67 billion.
